remaining_maintenance_text_check.subject: def-fd-x00
remaining_maintenance_text_check.actual_current_definition_passage: The vorticity field is $\operatorname{curl}u$. If $\gamma:[a,b]\to\Omega$ is a closed piecewise-$C^1$ oriented curve, with $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$, its circulation is $\oint_\gamma u\cdot d\mathbf r$. If $S$ is a compact oriented regular surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal $n_S$, its volume-flux observable is $\int_S u\cdot n_S\,dS$. The traction on $S$ is $\sigma n_S$ and the formal resultant force is the componentwise surface integral $\int_S\sigma n_S\,dS$. A steady velocity field is a map $u_0:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ for which $u(t,x)=u_0(x)$ for all $t\in I$ and $x\in\Omega$; a streamline of $u_0$ is a $C^1$ curve $x:J\to\Omega$ on a nondegenerate real interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ (open, closed, half-open or unbounded) satisfying $x'(s)=u_0(x(s))$. Here $C^1$ means that $x$ is continuous on $J$, is continuously differentiable on its interior, and at each included finite endpoint has the corresponding one-sided derivative to which the interior derivative extends continuously. The displayed equation is imposed in the interior and with that one-sided derivative at any included endpoint. The variable $s$ is a curve parameter, not time; no curve-existence assertion is made. A closed material loop on a time interval $J\subseteq I$ is a $C^1$ map $X:J\times[0,1]\to\Omega$ with $X(t,0)=X(t,1)$ and $\partial_tX(t,\theta)=u(t,X(t,\theta))$; the definition asserts no existence of such a map. For the following limit, an exterior spatial domain $\Omega$ means that there is $R_0>0$ such that $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|>R_0\}\subseteq\Omega$. For a scalar or vector field $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ or $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$, respectively, and $f_\infty$ in the same target space, $f(x)\to f_\infty$ uniformly in direction as $|x|\to\infty$ means $\sup_{|e|=1}|f(re)-f_\infty|\to0$ in the scalar case and $\sup_{|e|=1}\|f(re)-f_\infty\|_2\to0$ in the vector case, with $r\to\infty$.
